name: icloud-connector
description: Local access to your iCloud calendars, contacts and mail. Never sends anything. Messages only go to the Trash (never deleted permanently), your own events are deleted only after a backup.
long_description:
This connector runs entirely on your Mac (no server on the internet) and connects Claude to iCloud.

Calendar: read and search events, find free slots, create and change events, change a single occurrence of a series, move an event to another calendar (the original is removed only after the copy was created and read back; backed up as .ics first), and take over a calendar invitation from a mail as your own event (import_invitation: no attendees, no reply to the sender). There are no invitations or attendees. Shared calendars are only written to when you name the calendar explicitly. Deleting: the delete_event tool deletes only your own events, single events and whole recurring series. Before deleting, it backs up the event as an .ics file in ~/Library/Application Support/icloud-mcp/deleted/ (90 days, at most 200 files; double-clicking the file restores it in Apple Calendar) and returns it in full. Events with attendees, events organized by others, events in shared calendars and single occurrences of a series are never deleted, and the first three kinds are never moved either. iCloud itself cannot restore individual deleted events.

Contacts: search (also by address or group), read all details, list groups, see upcoming birthdays and anniversaries, create contacts (after a duplicate check) and change them with update_contact. Before every change the contact card is saved as a .vcf file in ~/Library/Application Support/icloud-mcp/contacts-backup/. Contacts and groups are never deleted.

Mail: folders, inbox and search, read messages, conversations and attachments (text, PDF text, calendar invitations; without marking anything as read), prepare replies, forwards (with the original's attachments) and drafts. Drafts are saved in the Drafts folder; you review and send them yourself in Apple Mail. The trash_message tool moves at most 20 messages per call to the Trash, after checking subject and sender. Nothing is ever deleted permanently; messages in the Trash can be restored for about 30 days. move_message moves up to 50 messages to another folder (never to the Trash, Drafts, Sent or Junk), set_message_flags marks up to 50 messages as read/unread or flagged. Both check id, subject and sender first. There is no sending.

Recommendation: in Claude Desktop (Settings > Extensions), set the deletion tools delete_event and trash_message and the tools update_event (it also covers moving an event to another calendar), update_contact, move_message and set_message_flags to require approval. Claude then asks before every deletion, change, move or marking, and scheduled tasks cannot run them on their own.

Your app-specific password is stored in the macOS Keychain.

tools.name: list_calendars
tools.description: List calendars (shared calendars are marked)

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: List events in a time range

tools.name: search_events
tools.description: Search events

tools.name: find_free_slots
tools.description: Find free slots

tools.name: create_event
tools.description: Create an event (no invitations)

tools.name: update_event
tools.description: Change an event or one occurrence of a series, or move it to another calendar (own events only, no attendees)

tools.name: delete_event
tools.description: Delete one of your own events (backed up as .ics first; never with attendees or in shared calendars)

tools.name: import_invitation
tools.description: Add a calendar invitation from a mail as your own event (no attendees, no reply)

tools.name: search_contacts
tools.description: Search contacts (name, company, email, phone, address; optionally by group)

tools.name: get_contact
tools.description: Get one contact with all details

tools.name: list_contact_groups
tools.description: List contact groups with member counts (read-only)

tools.name: upcoming_contact_dates
tools.description: Upcoming birthdays and anniversaries of contacts

tools.name: create_contact
tools.description: Create one contact (checks for duplicates first; never changes existing contacts)

tools.name: update_contact
tools.description: Change one contact (backed up as .vcf first; no deletion, no groups)

tools.name: list_mailboxes
tools.description: List mail folders

tools.name: unread_counts
tools.description: Count unread messages

tools.name: list_recent
tools.description: Latest messages in a folder

tools.name: search_messages
tools.description: Search messages

tools.name: get_message
tools.description: Read a message (paged, without marking it as read); lists attachments

tools.name: read_attachment
tools.description: Read one attachment (text, PDF text, calendar invitation); other types: metadata only

tools.name: get_thread
tools.description: Read a conversation

tools.name: create_draft
tools.description: Create a draft, reply draft or forward draft with the original's attachments (never sent)

tools.name: trash_message
tools.description: Move messages to the Trash (at most 20, never deleted permanently)

tools.name: move_message
tools.description: Move messages to another folder (at most 50; never to the Trash, Drafts, Sent or Junk)

tools.name: set_message_flags
tools.description: Mark messages read/unread or flagged/unflagged (at most 50)

tools.name: list_reminder_lists
tools.description: List the lists of Apple Reminders (open counts, default list)

tools.name: list_reminders
tools.description: List reminders (open, completed or all; due range)

tools.name: search_reminders
tools.description: Search reminders by title and notes

tools.name: create_reminder
tools.description: Create a reminder (due date, notes, priority, list)

tools.name: update_reminder
tools.description: Change a reminder (title is checked first; never deletes)

tools.name: complete_reminder
tools.description: Mark reminders completed or open again (at most 20; never deletes)

apple_id.title: Apple ID (email address)
apple_id.description: The email address of your Apple ID. It is the username for Calendar and Contacts.

mail_user.title: iCloud email address
mail_user.description: Your @icloud.com address, the username for Mail. It can differ from your Apple ID.

app_password.title: App-specific password
app_password.description: Create one at account.apple.com > Sign-In and Security > App-Specific Passwords. Not your regular Apple ID password.

timezone.title: Time zone
timezone.description: Time zone for events, e.g. Europe/Berlin.

default_calendar.title: Default calendar for new events
default_calendar.description: Name of a private, non-shared calendar that new events go to when no calendar is given. If empty, events are only created when a calendar is named.
